speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Prime Minister (a) over the past three years, how many reports have been made annually by consumers regarding unauthorised online bank transactions; (b) in what proportion of cases is there two-factor authentication (2FA) by token and SMS one-time password respectively; and (c) what is the recourse for consumers who suspect that they are victims of cybercrime or mobile device hacking leading to the unauthorised bank transactions.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: I think this really reflects the advent and the growing number of electronic transactions that we are seeing.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Many victims have been tricked into revealing their user IDs, passwords, OTPs or credit card details to scammers.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The Police and banks are following up on these cases and investigations are on-going.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Customers play an important part in preventing scams, because guarding against online threats starts with practising good cyber hygiene.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This includes keeping passwords secret and promptly updating the security patches and anti-virus software on computers and mobile devices.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: It is very important that consumers treat their online banking login information, including OTPs, as they would their ATM PINs.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We cannot emphasise this enough to the public.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Never reveal your login information, including OTPs, to others.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Employees of financial institutions will not ask for such information.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: So, if you are asked for it by a third party, do not provide it.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Consumers should also heed the security email advisories, notices and alerts disseminated by their banks, MAS, the Singapore Police Force and the National Crime Prevention Council, and share them with family and friends.
